official_path:
Official FRP recovery (try this first):
  1. Sign in with the Google account that was synced to this phone
     before the reset. If the password is forgotten, recover it at
     https://accounts.google.com/signin/recovery from another device.
  2. If the account cannot be recovered, take the phone plus proof
     of purchase (receipt, box with matching IMEI) to the
     manufacturer service centre or the carrier that sold it —
     Samsung, Google, Xiaomi and others remove FRP with proof.
  3. Only if both fail and the phone is yours: a partition-level
     erase of `frp` (see `openunlock frp erase --confirm`) removes
     the stored lock. It does not recover any data.

methods.name: TalkBack -> Help & Feedback -> YouTube -> Settings
methods.description: Enable TalkBack from the setup wizard, open its Help & Feedback page, follow a link into YouTube, then reach Settings from there and add a new Google account.
methods.applies_to: Android 5.0–9.0; some Samsung devices on Android 14/15
methods.patched_as_of: Android 10+ (most vendors); Samsung patched the share-sheet entry points in successive 2024–2026 updates

steps.text: In TalkBack settings, open Help & Feedback, tap a link to open YouTube, then from YouTube open Settings.
steps.desc: Follow the Help & Feedback link into YouTube
Open Settings (works once the TalkBack path has escaped the setup wizard)

steps.text: In Settings go to Accounts > Add account and add a Google account you own, then finish setup.
steps.desc: Add a Google account, then complete setup

methods.name: Emergency dialer -> notification shade -> Settings
methods.description: From the verification screen, open the emergency dialer, fill it with a long string, pull down the notification shade and reach Settings from there.
methods.patched_as_of: Android 9 (2018) — dialer no longer exposes the shade

steps.desc: Fill the dialer field with a long string

steps.text: Swipe down from the top to open the notification shade and tap the Settings gear icon.
steps.desc: Reach Settings from the notification shade

methods.name: Maps / YouTube intent -> share -> Settings
methods.description: Launch Google Maps or YouTube by intent from the setup flow, use the share sheet to reach a browser or Settings, and add an account from there.
methods.patched_as_of: Android 13+ — share-sheet entry points closed; Samsung closed most of them in One UI 5/6 updates

steps.text: From Maps/YouTube, use Share to open a browser, then navigate to Settings (or open the Galaxy Store).
steps.desc: Use the share sheet to escape to a browser/Settings

methods.name: Verification screen -> Forgot password -> browser
methods.description: On the Google verification screen choose 'Try another way', enter any address, tap 'Forgot password' — this opens a browser, from which Settings can be reached.
methods.patched_as_of: Android 13 — the forgot-password flow no longer opens a general browser

steps.desc: Open Google account recovery in the browser

steps.text: If a browser opens, use it to reach Settings (via the browser menu or a downloaded settings shortcut).
steps.desc: Escape from the browser to Settings

methods.name: Samsung setup-wizard share-sheet loophole (Android 15)
methods.description: Navigate the Samsung setup wizard in a specific sequence to reach accessibility settings, then use the share sheet to open Galaxy Store / YouTube and add an account.
methods.applies_to: Samsung Galaxy A/M-series, Android 15, patches up to early 2026
methods.patched_as_of: 2026 patches — S-series with the latest patches need other methods; share-sheet entry points are being closed build by build

steps.text: In the setup wizard, reach the accessibility settings via the wizard's own accessibility entry point.
steps.desc: Reach accessibility settings from the wizard

steps.text: Use the share sheet from an accessibility help page to open the Galaxy Store or YouTube, then install/open a settings shortcut and add a Google account.
steps.desc: Share-sheet escape to Galaxy Store / YouTube
